issue: सुनु सब कीसा: सब with ते (they are not all heroes) or with कीसा (listen, all you monkeys / monkey)
our reading: they are not all heroes; listen, monkey (Rāvaṇa addresses Aṅgada alone)
alternatives: birds cross the ocean, yet they are not heroes; listen, all you monkeys

issue: सीता मैं हारी: Aṅgada stakes Sītā as a wager
our reading: Śrī Rāma will turn back and I have lost Sītā (as a wager)
alternatives: I shall have lost (the cause of) Sītā; I give up claim to Sītā

issue: बिसमय: wonder or dismay (विषाद)?
our reading: wonder (विस्मय): the gods watch now in wonder, now in delight
alternatives: dismay/grief (खेद), as when the monkeys suffer

issue: Who is अकुलान, the she-crocodile or Hanumān?
our reading: the she-crocodile, in a frenzy, seized his foot
alternatives: then Hanumān was troubled (when seized)

issue: सब बिधि सुखद परम हित जानी: whom did Sumitrā know as giving joy and the greatest well-wisher?
our reading: Rāma: knowing me (Rāma) a source of joy in every way and your truest well-wisher
alternatives: Lakṣmaṇa: knowing you would give me every comfort and be my greatest good

issue: सहोदर literally 'of the same womb', though Lakṣmaṇa is Sumitrā's son
our reading: a brother of one's own blood
alternatives: full brother, born of the same mother (literal)

review: Agree with the doubt: the plain reading of the words is epithets, but Gita Press reads Devāntaka and Narāntaka; the owner should decide. The Hindi list leaves open whether the epithets qualify Durmukha, which the doubt already covers.
Agree with the doubt; the address reading (हे स्वामी / My lord) is the usual one and fits Kumbhakarṇa speaking to his king.
Agree with the doubt; the address to Vibhīṣaṇa reads naturally, the alternative is possible.
Agree with the doubt and with our reading (Kumbhakarṇa took him for dead, so Sugrīva slipped free).

issue: सुररिपु and मनुज अहारी: plain epithets ("foe of the gods", "eater of men") or the names Devāntaka and Narāntaka (Rāvaṇa's sons, slain earlier in the Vālmīki account)
our reading: plain epithets, as separate warriors
alternatives: Devāntaka and Narāntaka by name
epithets of Durmukha

issue: प्रभु: Kumbhakarṇa addressing Rāvaṇa ("my lord") or qualifying the god (that Lord, the god)
our reading: address to Rāvaṇa (हे स्वामी / My lord)
alternatives: you made enmity with that Lord, the god whose servants are Śiva, Brahmā and the gods

issue: बीर: address to Vibhīṣaṇa or qualifying Kumbhakarṇa himself (मैं कालबस बीर)
our reading: address to Vibhīṣaṇa (हे वीर / brave one)
alternatives: I, a warrior, have fallen under death

issue: निबुकि गयउ तेहि मृतक प्रतीती: Kumbhakarṇa believed Sugrīva dead, or Sugrīva slipped away like a dead thing
our reading: Sugrīva slipped free because Kumbhakarṇa believed him dead
alternatives: Sugrīva, as if dead, slid out of his armpit

issue: अरुन: whether 'red' goes with the lotus eyes (राजीव लोचन अरुन) or with the body reddened by drops of blood (अरुन तन सोनित कनी).
our reading: the lotus eyes are red; drops of blood are on the body
alternatives: lotus eyes; the body red with drops of blood

issue: बोले अंगदादि कपि नाना: बोले as 'spoke to' or 'called, summoned' (Awadhi बोलना = to call).
our reading: spoke to Aṅgada and many other monkeys
alternatives: summoned Aṅgada and many other monkeys

issue: सेन समेत रहेहु तीनिउ जन: stay with Lakṣmaṇa along with the army, or stay (here) with the army.
our reading: you three stay with the army
alternatives: you three go with him (Lakṣmaṇa) along with the army
you three stay behind here with the army

issue: जय अनंत: Ananta may be Lakṣmaṇa (Śeṣa, slayer of Meghanāda; cf. lanka.75.do75, 76.cau4) or Śrī Rāma, whose glory the gods are singing.
our reading: kept as Ananta, unidentified
alternatives: Lakṣmaṇa as Ananta
Śrī Rāma, the infinite

issue: नयसीला: qualifies Hanumān (मारुति) alone, or all those named
our reading: Hanumān, wise in counsel
alternatives: all of you, skilled in right counsel

issue: कहा न माना: whose words were not heeded (Mandodarī's own, or anyone's counsel)
our reading: you would not heed what you were told (anyone's counsel)
alternatives: you did not heed my words

issue: चरन रति अति निर्मली: Sītā's pure love for the feet of the Lord of Kosala, or an epithet of the Lord's feet
our reading: Sītā hails the Lord of Kosala, whose feet (adored by Śiva) she loves with a wholly pure love
alternatives: the Lord of Kosala, whose feet are adored by Śiva and loved with pure devotion (by all devotees)

issue: दूषन हा: slayer of the demon Dūṣaṇa, or destroyer of faults (दूषण = fault)
our reading: slayer of Dūṣaṇa
alternatives: destroyer of faults
both senses at once

issue: प्रथम प्रेम अनुमाना: Rāma considered Daśaratha's former love (from his earthly life), or Rāma first weighed his love
our reading: mindful of his father's love of old
alternatives: first perceiving his father's love, Rāma looked at him and gave him firm knowledge

issue: कालव्यालकरालभूषणधरं: काल in कालव्याल can be 'black' (MW kāla 1: black, dark; kāla-sarpa: the black, most venomous cobra) or 'Death' (deadly, Death-like).
our reading: serpents dreadful as Death (कालके समान भयंकर सर्प).
alternatives: black (deadly) cobras, fearsome as ornaments: काले रंगके भयंकर सर्पोंके गहने / adorned with dreadful black serpents.

issue: रावन मातु पिता: Apte (mālyavat) makes Mālyavān Rāvaṇa's maternal uncle, not his mother's father.
our reading: The verse itself says मातु पिता, Rāvaṇa's mother's father; our pieces follow the verse (रावणकी माताका पिता / the father of Rāvaṇa's mother).
alternatives: Mother's elder kinsman (grand-uncle, as in the Vālmīki genealogy, where Mālyavān is the brother of Kaikasī's father Sumālī); Apte's 'maternal uncle'.

issue: Line 4 'जहँ सो तहँ निसिचर हए': सो may mean the hurled rock (सैल) rather than the demon.
our reading: The demons are slain wherever they stand (H3/E3 take सो as the demon).
alternatives: Wherever the rock lands, there the demons are killed (सो = the सैल just named).

issue: सुररिपु and मनुज अहारी: epithets or names. Monier-Williams lists Devāntaka and Narāntaka as Rakṣasas in the Rāmāyaṇa (narāntaka also means 'destroyer of men'), so names are possible; the words Tulsidas uses (सुररिपु 'foe of the gods', मनुज अहारी 'eater of men') are not those names, only close to their sense.
our reading: plain epithets, as separate warriors
alternatives: Devāntaka and Narāntaka by name
epithets of Durmukha

issue: करौं अजय मख: अजय (MW/Apte 'unconquered, invincible') may qualify the sacrifice itself ('an unfailing, unconquerable sacrifice') or name its fruit ('a sacrifice that makes me invincible').
our reading: a sacrifice that would make him invincible
alternatives: I will perform an unconquerable (unfailing) sacrifice

issue: रन रंगा: the zest of battle, or the battle-arena (raṅga = arena, stage in MW/Apte)?
our reading: in the fervour of battle (रणकी उमंगमें)
alternatives: in the arena of battle (रणभूमिमें)
the sport/spectacle of battle

issue: समरूप: MW gives only 'of the same form'; our glossary has 'सदा एक-सा रूप | uniform, unchanging', while the published piece (after review) reads 'the same towards all' (impartial). The two disagree.
our reading: the same towards all (सम = alike, impartial); Hindi keeps समरूप
alternatives: of one unvarying form (the dictionary sense; overlaps with सदा एकरस in the same line)
both: the same in form and the same towards all

issue: सुजान रायँ: 'king among the wise' or 'the wise king'
our reading: ज्ञानियोंके राजा | king among the wise (सुजान = Skt. sujña 'knowing well' as the first member of a tatpuruṣa)
alternatives: सुजान as an adjective of राय: 'the all-knowing King' (karmadhāraya); neither MW nor Apte lists सुजान, so grammar alone leaves both open
